title: Three Springs and One Short Hinge
subtitle: 遗产保护 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 遗产保护（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化遗产与保护）
meta: 主题语境：遗产保护（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化遗产与保护）　|　核心词汇：gate　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 gate 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the keeper ① opened a gate that no visitor in the town would have described, and he said the opening was the whole of the spring. The ② gate, meaning the doors themselves and not the wall, ran three springs and stayed undescribed in the book; a gate, he said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ gate in that town had the same short hinge beside it, and the ④ gate at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A gate, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the keeper said the describing is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the gate was the whole of the matter, meaning the barrier and not the doors. The ⑥ gate, meaning the barrier and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; gate, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a door and a barrier. He said the barrier is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ gate had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short hinge. The ⑧ gate of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in November, was one town and three springs of describing; gate, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ gate I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the town. A ⑩ gate, my mother said in 1973, is the only one that improves by being described; every gate, she said, is a barrier that has agreed to look like a door. She said the barrier was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 大门；城门（指城里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 大门；城门（指那些门扇本身，与围墙相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a gate 打开一座大门
D. n. 大门（指留给孩子们走的那一座）
E. n. 门（抽象总称，指一座城门之事）
F. n. 大门（指测绘图里标出、被丈量过的那座）
G. n. 闸门；登机口（指一件事里人人都过却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 关口（抽象总称，指人人都过却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: opened a gate that no visitor in the town would have described
The gate, meaning the doors themselves and not the wall
the gate at the far end
the gate was the whole of the matter
the gate had become a line in a plan
The gate of the whole thing
A gate, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: open a gate 意为“打开一座大门”，1963 年那位守门人打开了城里没有一位游客肯描述的一座门。
gate 意为“大门、城门”，指那些门扇本身而不是围墙，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被描述。
gate 意为“大门、城门”，指城里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一副矮矮的铰链。
gate 意为“大门”，指最远端留给孩子们走的那一座，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
gate 意为“闸门、关口”，指一件事里人人都过却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这道关口就是那件事的全部。
gate 意为“关口”，指人人都过却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座大门，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
gate 意为“大门”，指测绘图里标出、被丈量过的那座，到 1969 年这一座成了图纸里的一行。
gate 意为“门”，守门人十一月写道，整件事的城门之事是一座城和三个春天的描述。
gate 意为“大门”，我记得的是图纸里描述过的那座，1971 年关上了，至今仍被说成城里最安静的一座。
gate 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，一座大门是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
